title: Another Jesus, A Different Spirit, A Different Gospel
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: The Nature of the Counterfeit
subpoints: The most dangerous lies are those that resemble the truth
False apostles deny the truth by substituting it with something 'better'
The serpent's method: offering an alternative to God's word

outline.title: Another Jesus
subpoints: False teachers emphasize power, eloquence, and success
Paul preached a Jesus who achieved glory through suffering and the cross
A Jesus without the cross cannot save; the cross is central to the gospel

outline.title: A Different Spirit
subpoints: The true Spirit produces fruit: love, peace, gentleness, and humility
The false spirit is authoritarian, overbearing, and self-exalting
The source of the false spirit is Satan, disguised as a minister of righteousness

outline.title: A Different Gospel
subpoints: The false gospel stresses power and glory while omitting the crucified Christ
The true gospel is defined by Christ dying for sins and rising again
The message of the cross may seem weak to the world but is of first importance

outline.title: Practical Application
subpoints: Know the real Jesus: crucified and risen
Test every message by asking: 'Where is the cross?'
Do not bear with counterfeit ministries or gospels

summary:
In this afternoon service, Pastor Tito Lyro continues the sermon series on 2 Corinthians by examining verse 4, where Paul warns the Corinthian church against accepting 'another Jesus, a different spirit, or a different gospel.' The sermon highlights that the most dangerous counterfeits are those that closely resemble the truth, much like the serpent's deception of Eve. The false apostles in Corinth were not denying Jesus outright but were substituting a version of Him that emphasized power, eloquence, and success while omitting the suffering and death of the cross. This 'another Jesus' is contrasted with the true Christ, who achieved glory through the cross, a truth that remains central to the authentic gospel today.

The message further distinguishes between the Holy Spirit and the spirit of the false teachers. The Holy Spirit produces fruit such as love, peace, and humility, pointing believers toward Christ. In contrast, the spirit of the false apostles is described as authoritarian, overbearing, and self-exalting, ultimately sourced from Satan. Paul’s ministry, by comparison, was marked by meekness and gentleness, using authority for edification rather than destruction.

Finally, the sermon addresses the 'different gospel' preached by these opponents, which stressed power and glory while neglecting the crucified Lord. This is contrasted with the true gospel, summarized in 1 Corinthians 15, which centers on Christ dying for sins and rising again. Believers are challenged to test all messages and ministries by the presence of the cross and the fruit of the Spirit, refusing to bear with counterfeit teachings that compromise the purity of the gospel.
